binders: There exists a real number C.
For the same C, universally quantify over every type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
Universally quantify over every measure mu on Omega carrying an IsProbabilityMeasure mu instance.
Universally quantify over every real number a.
hypotheses: The measure mu is assumed to be a probability measure through the displayed typeclass instance.
conclusions: For every displayed probability-measure setting and real a, LocalDef001 mu (the constant function with value a) <= ENNReal.ofReal(C * |a|).

Equivalently after unfolding the local definitions, the infimum of all t in ENNReal for which the constant function is measurable, t != 0, t != top, exp(a^2/(t.toReal)^2) is mu-integrable, and its mu-integral is <= 2 is at most ENNReal.ofReal(C * |a|).
mathematical_definitions: For a real-valued X, let A(mu,X) be the set of t in ENNReal such that X is measurable, t is neither 0 nor top, omega maps to exp((X omega)^2/(t.toReal)^2) is mu-integrable, and its mu-integral is at most 2.
LocalDef001 mu X = LocalDef002 mu X = sInf A(mu,X) in the complete order ENNReal.
ENNReal.ofReal(r) is the ENNReal embedding of the nonnegative part of r.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is one universal real constant C >= 1 such that, on every measurable space with every probability measure mu and for every real a, the infimum exponential-moment scale of the constant function X(omega) = a is no greater than the extended-nonnegative-real value of C|a|. The admissible finite nonzero scales t are exactly those for which X is measurable, exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is integrable, and its integral is at most 2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition concerns only constant real-valued functions, despite ranging over arbitrary measurable spaces and probability measures.
The existential C precedes every space, measure, and scalar quantifier, so a single C must work uniformly in all cases.
The statement bounds an infimum; it neither chooses an admissible scale nor asserts that the infimum is attained or itself admissible.
Admissible scales explicitly exclude 0 and top, but their infimum may still be a boundary value such as 0.
When a = 0, the right side is 0, so the target forces the scale infimum for the zero constant function to be 0.
ENNReal.ofReal truncates negative inputs. Here C >= 1 and |a| >= 0 ensure that C|a| is nonnegative, but the formal truncating map remains part of the statement.
The target does not separately assert that a probability measure exists on every measurable type; universal quantification through a typeclass has no instance to check when none exists.
D003 separately demands integrability before using the integral bound, so any default convention of the Bochner integral for nonintegrable functions cannot by itself make a scale admissible.
The conversion t.toReal occurs only for scales constrained to be neither 0 nor top; without those conjuncts, boundary conversion and division-by-zero behavior would be consequential.

No nonemptiness of the admissible-scale set is stated explicitly. Through the complete ENNReal order, its sInf is nevertheless a total value, with an empty-set case potentially producing top and making a finite upper bound impossible.
ambiguities: The packet gives IsProbabilityMeasure only as an external-frontier proposition/typeclass without its constructors or fields, so the exact internal normalization equation is not unfolded beyond the mathematical assertion that mu is a probability measure.

Several structural instance bodies contain elided proof fields. They suffice to identify the selected standard orders, norms, topology, integral, and arithmetic operations, but the packet does not expose those proof terms; no additional proposition-level assumptions are visible.
